extracted.intended_audience: readers/owners of The Art of Computer Programming; potential purchasers; experts invited to beta-test fascicles; people who might report errata
extracted.subtask_description: Policies and practical guidance from Don Knuth about authorized eBook formats, how and when to report errors, rewards for finding mistakes, availability/formats of errata, beta-test fascicles and how readers can help, and resources for running example programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized eBook format and quality
rubrics_metrics.description: These volumes are now available also in portable electronic form, using PDF format. Special care has been taken to make the search feature work well. Some non-PDF versions have also appeared, against my recommendations, and those versions are frankly quite awful. Some non-PDF versions also masquerade as PDF. The authorized PDF versions can be purchased at www.informit.com/taocp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not purchase eTAOCP in Kindle format if you expect the mathematics to make sense. (The ePUB format may be just as bad.) If you have been misled into purchasing one of these inferior versions, the publishers have told me that they will replace your copy with the PDF edition that I have personally approved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Error-reporting eligibility (what to report to the author vs publisher)
rubrics_metrics.description: Please do not tell me about errors that you find in an eBook, whether it's PDF or not, unless the same errors are present in a printed copy; such mistakes should be reported directly to the publisher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only report to the author errors that are also present in printed copies. Errors that appear only in non-authorized eBook editions (or eBook-only mistakes) should be reported to the publisher, not to Don Knuth.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to send errata / required format and contact info
rubrics_metrics.description: Please send your comments either by email to taocp@cs.stanford.edu or by old-fashioned mail to Donald E. Knuth ... In either case please include your postal address, so that I can mail an official certificate of deposit as a token of thanks for any improvements to which you have contributed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send PLAIN ASCII TEXT ONLY. Do not include attachments of any kind; your message should be readable on brand-X operating systems for all values of X. (Encrypted messages that I get from "gmail.com" are also gibberish and unreadable without great pain.) BUT PLEASE DO NOT SEND EMAIL TO TAOCP EXCEPT TO REPORT ERRORS IN THE ART OF COMPUTER PROGRAMMING. Although I'm working full time on Volume 4C these days, I will try to reply to all such messages within nine months of receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rewards for finding errors and what is rewarded
rubrics_metrics.description: The first finder of any error in my books receives 0x$1.00 ($2.56), deposited to their account at the Bank of San Serriffe; significant suggestions are also worth 0x$0.20 ($0.32) each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you are a really careful reader, you may be able to recoup more than the cost of the books this way. However, people who have read Eats, Shoots & Leaves should not expect a reward for criticizing the ways in which I use commas. Punctuation is extremely important to me, but I insist on doing it my own way. Similarly, you can save yourself valuable time by not trying to get me to change ‘awhile’ to ‘a while’.

rubrics_metrics.name: Errata and addenda availability, formats, and update policy
rubrics_metrics.description: There are detailed Errata et Addenda lists for each volume and fascicle; errata files are provided in compressed PostScript, long form PostScript, and TeX form. Some lists are archival and are not being kept up to date; other errata lists have last-updated dates noted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have no way to look at compressed PostScript files, you might try reading the TeX code as a last resort; note that some TeX files import private files and cannot be run through TeX, but they still let you figure out page numbers where corrections have been made. Errata files include dates and sizes; check the 'after 2021' / 'earliest errata' / 'long form' entries as appropriate for the volume.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beta-test fascicles: publication process and solicitation of expert feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: New material for Volume 4 will first appear in beta-test form as fascicles of approximately 128 pages each, issued approximately twice per year. These fascicles represent my best attempt to write a comprehensive account; but computer science has grown to the point where I cannot hope to be an authority on all the material covered in these books. Therefore I'll need feedback from readers in order to prepare the official volumes later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fascicles are put online primarily so that experts in the field can check the contents before they are released more widely. If you want to help debug them, please go right ahead (i.e., read the fascicle, check details, and send corrections via the errata procedure). Pre-fascicles and 'alpha-testing' pre-fascicles may be available for early expert review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducing and running example programs: MIX/MMIX and MIXware resources
rubrics_metrics.description: The MIX computer will soon be replaced by a RISC machine called MMIX. Meanwhile if you want to try out the existing programs for the original 60s-era machine, you might be able to find suitable software at the following sites: GNU's MIX Development Kit, JMixSim, MixIDE, MIXBuilder, EMIX, MIX/MIXAL in C, David Smallberg's version, Dan Taflin's assembler/simulator in HTML and Javascript, Andras Pahi's updated version of Darius Bacon and Eric Raymond's assembler/simulator, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the listed emulators, assemblers, and simulators to run or test the book's example programs. For modern work, MMIX replaces MIX; Martin Ruckert's MMIX Supplement translates MIX programs into MMIX form and is recommended for instruction and self-study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof required for alleged typographic errors in quotations and bibliographic citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerous quotations and bibliographic citations found in these books have been copied verbatim from the original sources. If you believe you have found a typographic error, you must prove it by showing that the original was incorrectly transcribed; believe it or not, your language has changed over the years, just as English has.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting what you think is a transcription error in a quoted original, include evidence from the original source demonstrating that the passage was copied incorrectly rather than reflecting historical/orthographic differences.
